title: Chapter 1: International Relations
content:
🌸 ሰላም ውድ የ EthioFresh ተማሪዎች!
እንኳን ወደ Global Trends (Global Affairs) የመጀመሪያው ምዕራፍ ቱቶሪያል በደህና መጣችሁ! በዛሬው የ Chapter 1 Part 1 የትምህርት ክፍላችን የሞጁሉን መግቢያ፣ 1.1 Conceptualizing Nationalism, Nations and States እና 1.2 Understanding International Relations በዝርዝር፣ በስፋት እና በጥልቀት እንመለከታለን። ይህ ኖት በ EthioFresh የትምህርት አዘጋጆች ለእናንተ የተዘጋጀ ሲሆን፣ ሌላ ተጨማሪ ሞጁል ወይም ኖት ሳያስፈልጋችሁ ለፈተና 100% አዘጋጅቶ A+ እንድታመጡ ታስቦ የቀረበ ነው። መልካም ጥናት!

Introduction

International relations as presented in daily news concerns a vast number of disparate events: political leaders meeting in summits, international negotiations being concluded, wars breaking out, acts of terror being committed, and economic sanctions being imposed. To make sense of this overwhelming flow of information, we need to understand the contemporary world, its history, and how these disparate events hang together. The academic study of international politics aims to radically simplify this messy reality. Rather than focusing merely on the daily news flow, IR focuses on the fundamental principles underlying world politics.

ዓለም አቀፍ ግንኙነት በየቀኑ በዜና እንደምናየው እጅግ በርካታ የተበታተኑ ክስተቶችን (የመሪዎች ስብሰባ፣ የዲፕሎማሲ ድርድሮች፣ የጦርነቶች መነሳት፣ የሽብር ጥቃቶች እና የኢኮኖሚ ማዕቀቦች) ያካተተ ነው። የትምህርቱ ዋና አላማ እነዚህን የተበታተኑና ውስብስብ የዓለም ክስተቶች በጥልቀት በመተንተን፣ ከጀርባቸው ያሉትን መሠረታዊ የፖለቲካ እና የዲፕሎማሲ መርሆች (Basic Principles) በቀላሉ እንድንረዳ ማድረግ ነው።

1.1 Conceptualizing Nationalism, Nations and States

A. The Concept and Power of Nationalism

Nationalism is considered the most influential force in modern international affairs. Historically, it has been the primary catalyst for the outbreak of major revolutions and global wars, leading directly to the collapse of age-old empires, reshaping political borders, and fostering the emergence of new sovereign states. Nationalism's ultimate triumph is the establishment of the 'nation-state' as the key actor, legitimate authority, and primary political entity in world politics. According to Andrew Heywood (2014), nationalism is defined as the doctrine that asserts the nation as the basic political unit in organizing human society.

🔥 ብሔረተኝነት (Nationalism) በአለም አቀፍ ፖለቲካ ውስጥ ትልቁ እና ተፅዕኖ ፈጣሪው የፖለቲካ ኃይል ነው። በታሪክ አጋጣሚዎች የታላላቅ ኢምፓየሮች መደርመስ፣ የአዳዲስ ሀገራት መፈጠር እና የድንበሮች መከለል ዋና ምክንያት ነው። የብሔረተኝነት ትልቁ ስኬት 'Nation-State' (ብሔር-መንግስት) በአለም ፖለቲካ ውስጥ ዋና እና ህጋዊ ተዋናይ እንዲሆን ማድረጉ ነው። በፖለቲካ ሳይንሰኛው Heywood (2014) ብያኔ መሠረት፣ ብሔረተኝነት ማለት "ብሔር (Nation) የህብረተሰብ መዋቅር ዋናው እና መሠረታዊው የፖለቲካ አካል (Basic political unit) ነው" ብሎ የሚያምን የፖለቲካ እምነት/ዶክትሪን ነው።

B. Distinguishing Nation, State, and Country

In common parlance, the terms 'nation', 'state', and 'country' are frequently used interchangeably, but in political science, this is strictly incorrect. For example, the term 'United Nations' is a misnomer because it is actually an association or society of states, not nations. Similarly, referring to 'the Chinese', 'the Americans', or 'the Russians' merely as 'nations' is imprecise.

According to Heywood (2014), nations are historical entities that evolve organically out of similar ethnic communities, revealing themselves through shared identity, myths, legends, and cultural songs. At the end of the 18th century, the 'state' was combined with the 'nation' to form the compound concept—the 'nation-state'. The nation constitutes a community joined by a shared identity and social practices. As nationalist leaders argued, the nation should take over the state and use its institutional structures for national ends. Thus, the nation added an interior life or 'soul' to the physical body of the early modern state machinery.

📌 በዕለታዊ አነጋገር 'Nation' (ብሔር)፣ 'State' (መንግስት/ሀገር) እና 'Country' የሚሉትን ቃላት እንቀላቅላቸዋለን፤ ነገር ግን በፖለቲካ ሳይንስ ይሄ በፍፁም ስህተት ነው!
• United Nations (UN): ስሙ 'United Nations' ቢባልም በይዘቱ ግን የ States (የመንግስታት/ሀገራት) ስብስብ እንጂ የ ብሔሮች (Nations) ስብስብ አይደለም። ስለዚህ ስሙ Misnomer (ስህተት) ይባላል።
• Nation (ብሔር): በታሪክ ሂደት ከተመሳሳዩ የብሔረሰብ ማህበረሰብ (Ethnic community) የበቀለ፣ በጋራ ማንነት፣ በባህል፣ በወግ፣ በታሪክ እና በዘፈኖች የሚገለፅ ማህበራዊ ማንነት ነው።
• Nation-State: በ 18ኛው ክፍለ ዘመን መጨረሻ ላይ 'Nation' እና 'State' ተዋሃዱ። ብሔር (Nation) ለመንግስት መዋቅር (State) መንፈስና ህይወት (Soul) የሰጠ አካል ነው።

C. Historical Evolution: Revolutions and Self-Determination

The historical evolution of nationalism and nation-states developed through major global milestones:

  • The American Revolution (1776): Introduced the preamble 'We the People of the United States', radically shifting political legitimacy from kings to the collective people.
  • The French Revolution (1789): Overthrew the old monarchical regime, stripped the aristocracy and church of absolute power, and declared that the French nation was governed by the people based on liberté, égalité, et fraternité (liberty, equality, and brotherhood).
  • The Congress of Vienna (1815): Attempted to restore Europe to its pre-revolutionary imperial order after the Napoleonic Wars, but nationalist sentiments continued to grow across the continent.
  • The Principle of Self-Determination: In the early 19th century, nationalism manifested as a liberal sentiment advocating for self-determination—the right of a people to determine their own political fate. This directly threatened the legitimacy of multi-ethnic empires.
  • 1848 Revolutions & National Unifications: Nationalist uprisings swept across Europe. Ethnic communities demanded statehood (e.g., Finns wanting an independent Finland, Bulgarians an independent Bulgaria, Serbs an independent Serbia). In 1861, Italy—previously divided into city-states and ruled by the Church—unified into a single nation-state.
  • 1918 (End of WWI): Self-determination was universally acknowledged as a right, leading to the collapse of empires and the formal redrawing of Europe into nation-states.
  • Coining of 'Inter-national': The term 'inter-national' was coined in 1783 by British philosopher Jeremy Bentham to describe relations between nation-states, replacing the older Westphalian inter-state model.
  • Contemporary Debates: Today, the role of nation-states is challenged by globalization, yet there is a marked revival of nationalism driven by religion and ethnicity. This is highlighted in Samuel P. Huntington's 'Clash of Civilizations' thesis, which countered Francis Fukuyama's 'End of History' thesis.

📜 የናሽናሊዝም ታሪካዊ ዕድገት ደረጃዎች፦
1. የአሜሪካ አብዮት (1776)፦ ህገ-መንግስቱ "We the People" በማለት የስልጣን ባለቤቱ ህዝብ መሆኑን አወጀ።
2. የፈረንሳይ አብዮት (1789)፦ የንጉሱን፣ ቤተ-ክርስቲያኑን እና የሀብታሞቹን የፖለቲካ የበላይነት በመሻር የፈረንሳይ ህዝብ በነፃነት፣ እኩልነት እና ወንድማማችነት (liberté, égalité, fraternité) እንዲመራ አደረገ።
3. የቪየና ኮንግረስ (1815)፦ ከናፖሊዮን ጦርነት በኋላ የቀደመውን የንጉሳዊ ስርዓት ለመመለስ ቢሞክርም የብሔረተኝነትን ስሜት ማስቆም አልተቻለም።
4. የራስን እድል በራስ መወሰን (Self-Determination)፦ ህዝቦች የራሳቸውን የፖለቲካ እድል በራሳቸው የመወሰን መብት እንዳላቸው የሚያምን የሊበራል እምነት ነው።
5. የ 1848 አብዮቶች እና የ 1861 የጣሊያን መዋሃድ፦ ፊንላንዶች፣ ቡልጋሪያውያን እና ሰርቦች ነፃነት ጠየቁ፤ ጣሊያንም በ 1861 ተዋሃደች።
6. 1918 (ከ 1ኛው የዓለም ጦርነት በኋላ)፦ Self-determination እንደ ህጋዊ መብት ተቀባይነት አገኘ።
7. Jeremy Bentham፦ 'Inter-national' የሚለውን ቃል በ 1783 ፈጠረ።
8. ወቅታዊ ሁኔታ፦ የሳሙኤል ሀንቲንግተን 'Clash of Civilizations' የፍራንሲስ ፉኩያማን 'End of History' ንድፈ-ሀሳብ በመሞገት የባህል እና ሃይማኖት ብሔረተኝነት ማንሰራራቱን ገልጿል።

😅 EthioFresh Humor Break:
የግቢ ህይወትና የዓለም ፖለቲካ! የዶርማችሁ ተማሪዎች ተሰብስበው "እኛ የዶርም 12 ተማሪዎች ህጋዊ መብታችን ተከብሮ የጽዳት ተራችንን በራሳችን እንወስናለን!" ካሉ ይሄ Self-determination ይባላል! ነገር ግን ዩናይትድ ኔሽንስ (UN) የብሔሮች ስብስብ ሳይሆን የመንግስታት (States) ስብስብ መሆኑን ካልያዛችሁ ፈተና ላይ False ብላችሁ ስትወጡ እንዳታቀረቅሩ! 😄
💡 Exam Hint (የፈተና ጥንቃቄዎች):
• Jeremy Bentham: 'inter-national' የሚለውን ቃል የተጠቀመበት ዓመት 1783 ሲሆን፣ 'International Relations' የሚለውን ትምህርት ስያሜ የተጠቀመው ደግሞ በ 1798 ነው! (ፈተና ላይ Matching ወይም True/False ላይ ይመጣል!)
• Huntington vs. Fukuyama: S.P. Huntington 'Clash of Civilizations' (የሲቪላይዜሽኖች ግጭት) ሲሆን Francis Fukuyama ደግሞ 'End of History' (የታሪክ ማብቂያ) ነው። አይቀላቀሉባችሁ!

1.2 Understanding International Relations

A. Everyday Life and Inescapable Interconnectedness

International relations is not merely an abstract academic discipline studied at universities; it is an integral aspect of our daily lives. Modern human existence is so interconnected geographically, intellectually, and socially that isolation is impossible. The module highlights explicit real-world examples demonstrating how ordinary actions carry international dimensions:

  • Cultural Participation: An Ethiopian student watching American sitcoms like Friends or Australian soap operas like Neighbors is participating in and learning about foreign cultures.
  • Travel and Environment: Flying from Addis Ababa to Washington DC or London subjects an individual to international air space agreements and contributes to global warming.
  • Economic Decisions: Purchasing fair-trade coffee is a direct decision contributing to foreign state and community development.
  • Employment and Corporate Governance: Working for an international corporation or a local Ethiopian business involves dealing with regional laws, international trade laws, employment codes, and tax treaties.
  • Public Global Events: Selecting an Olympic host city, awarding an Oscar, global warming conferences, and international crime combatting directly shape global political relations.
Principle of Inescapability: Participation in international relations is inescapable. No individual, nation, or state can exist in 'splendid isolation' or master its own fate independently. Even a giant superpower cannot compel everyone to do its bidding without external cooperation, trade, and diplomatic engagement.

🌐 ዓለም አቀፍ ግንኙነት (IR) በየቀኑ በህይወታችን ውስጥ ያለ ጉዳይ እንጂ የንድፈ-ሀሳብ ትምህርት ብቻ አይደለም። ማንም ሰው ወይም ሀገር ለብቻው ተነጥሎ (In splendid isolation) መኖር አይችልም።
በሞጁሉ የተጠቀሱት ተግባራዊ ምሳሌዎች (100% Exam Mandatory Examples)፦
1. ባህላዊ ትስስር፦ አንድ የኢትዮጵያ ተማሪ Friends ወይም Neighbors የተባሉ የውጭ ፊልሞችን/ሲትኮሞችን ሲመለከት ከዓለም አቀፍ ባህል ጋር ይገናኛል።
2. ጉዞና አካባቢ፦ ከአዲስ አበባ ወደ ዋሺንግተን ዲሲ ወይም ለንደን ሲበር የአየር ክልል ስምምነቶችን ያከብራል፤ በዓለም አየር ንብረት (Global Warming) ላይም አስተዋፅኦ ያደርጋል።
3. ንግድና ምርት፦ 'Fair-trade coffee' ሲገዛ ለሌሎች ሀገራት ልማት አስተዋፅኦ ያደርጋል።
4. ስራና ኩባንያ፦ በሀገር ውስጥም ሆነ በውጭ ኩባንያ ሲሰራ ከአለም አቀፍ የንግድ፣ የስራ እና የታክስ ህጎች ጋር ይገናኛል።
5. የኦሊምፒክ እና ኦስካር ዝግጅቶች፦ በህዝባዊ ኩነቶች አማካኝነት በሀገራት መካከል የፖለቲካ እና ዲፕሎማሲ ግንኙነት ይፈጠራል።

B. Academic Emergence of International Relations

Historically, the study of international relations was viewed merely as a branch of law, philosophy, or history. The term 'international relations' was first used by Jeremy Bentham in 1798. However, following the catastrophic carnage of World War I, scholars recognized the urgent need to understand how to prevent global conflict. Consequently, the first academic university chair of International Relations was established in 1919 at the University of Wales. Today, IR describes interactions between individuals, groups, firms, states, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), and intergovernmental organizations (IGOs).

🎓 የ IR የትምህርት ዘርፍ ታሪካዊ አመጣጥ፦
• ጥንት IR እንደ ህግ፣ ፈላስፋ እና ታሪክ ትምህርት አካል ተደርጎ ይታይ ነበር።
• Jeremy Bentham: በ 1798 'International Relations' የሚለውን ጽንሰ-ሀሳብ ለመጀመሪያ ጊዜ ተጠቀመ።
• ከ 1ኛው የዓለም ጦርነት እልቂት በኋላ በ 1919 በ University of Wales የመጀመሪያው የ IR ዩኒቨርሲቲ ወንበር (University Chair of IR) ተመሠረተ።

C. Domestic Politics vs. International Politics

There are profound legal, political, and social structural differences separating domestic politics from international politics:
FeatureDomestic Politics (የሀገር ውስጥ ፖለቲካ)International Politics (ዓለም አቀፍ ፖለቲካ)
Authority & PowerCentral government holds a monopoly on the legitimate use of physical force.No central authority exists; Anarchical structure operating on 'Self-Help'.
Law EnforcementPolice and judicial courts enforce laws and impose direct sanctions.Rely on competing legal systems with no central enforcement body.
Sense of CommunityShared national loyalty, common sense of justice and legitimacy.Divided loyalties; conflict and disagreement lie at the very heart of interactions.
Domestic Crises Becoming International: Domestic matters often cross borders and dominate the international political agenda. Health crises such as Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) and Avian Flu (ወፍ በሽታ) illustrate how purely domestic incidents trigger foreign policy changes and international commitments.

⚖️ በሀገር ውስጥ እና በዓለም አቀፍ ፖለቲካ መካከል ያሉ ልዩነቶች፦
1. የስልጣን ማዕከል፦ በሀገር ውስጥ ህግ አስከባሪ ማዕከላዊ መንግስት እና ፖሊስ አለ፤ በዓለም አቀፍ ፖለቲካ ግን ማዕከላዊ መንግስት የለም (Anarchy)። ስለሆነም ስርዓቱ 'Self-Help' (እያንዳንዱ ሀገር ራሱን በራሱ የሚረዳበት) ነው።
2. የህግ ማስከበር፦ በሀገር ውስጥ ፍርድ ቤትና ፖሊስ ሲኖር፤ በዓለም አቀፍ ደረጃ ግን አስገዳጅ ማዕከላዊ አካል የለም።
3. የሀገር ውስጥ ክስተቶች ወደ ዓለም አቀፍነት መቀየር፦ እንደ SARS እና Avian Flu (የወፍ በሽታ) ያሉ የጤና ወረርሽኞች የሀገር ውስጥ ጉዳይ ሆነው ተጀምረው የሀገራትን የውጭ ፖሊሲ (Foreign Policy) እስከ መቀየር ደርሰዋል።

D. Box 1.1: Philosophical Debates on Human Nature (Hobbes vs. Locke)

The theoretical perspectives in IR are grounded in 17th-century philosophical disputes regarding human nature:

  • Thomas Hobbes (1651): In his work Leviathan, Hobbes asserted that the natural state of human society is a state of "continual fear, and danger of violent death; and the life of man, solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short." This pessimistic assessment serves as the foundational cornerstone for Realist assumptions in IR, viewing the international system as dangerous, competitive, and state-centric.
  • John Locke: Provided an optimistic counter-perspective, arguing that sociability is the strongest bond between humans. Under natural law, human beings are equal, sociable, and free. Locke argued that society and order are possible even without an overarching coercive government, founding the core tenets of the Liberal/Idealist perspective in IR.
Adjustment of Power & Coercion: International politics involves achieving group ends against opposition through the delicate adjustment of power. A prominent example of physical force and coercion in international affairs is the 2003 invasion of Iraq by a US-led coalition of the willing. However, non-violent diplomatic mechanisms are also increasingly utilized.

🧠 የሆብስ እና የሎክ የፍልስፍና ክርክር (Realist vs Liberal Basis)፦
1. Thomas Hobbes (1651)፦ የሰው ልጅ ተፈጥሮ በጥርጣሬና በስጋት የተሞላ ነው ይላል። ህይወትም "solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short" (ብቸኛ፣ ደሃ፣ አሰቃቂ፣ አረመኔያዊ እና አጭር) ናት ብሎ ያምናቸዋል። ይህም ለ Realism (ሪያሊዝም) ቲዮሪ መሠረት ሆነ።
2. John Locke፦ ተስፋ ሰጪ እይታ አለው። ሰዎች በተፈጥሯቸው እኩል፣ ነፃ እና ማህበራዊ ናቸው፤ ያለ አስገዳጅ ኃይልም በስምምነት መኖር ይችላሉ ይላል። ይህም ለ Liberalism (ሊበራሊዝም) መሠረት ተጣለ።
3. የኃይል እርምጃ ምሳሌ፦ በ 2003 ዓ.ም በአሜሪካ መሪነት በኢራቅ ላይ የተካሄደው ወረራ (2003 Invasion of Iraq) በዓለም ፖለቲካ ውስጥ የኃይል እና የማስገደድ (Coercion & Physical Force) ትልቅ ምሳሌ ነው።

E. Maintaining International Order & The Expanding Arena

Maintaining order in an anarchic world requires complex bargaining and international organizations. The international arena has expanded dramatically since 1800:

  • In 1800, zero formal international organizations existed.
  • When the United Nations (UN) Charter was signed in October 1945, there were 51 founding member states.
  • By the early 21st century, UN membership grew to between 189 and 192 member states.
Global Interdependence: Today, citizens, businesses, and states rely on each other (and their rivals) across borders for ideas, goods, and services. Despite non-violent options, power, coercion, and strategic bargaining remain central to international political dynamics.
